reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger rather than trusting the handoff message. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly. Next I'll check the orders to confirm the refunds are consistent with them before relying on net_balance.

The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is below its order amount (272: 8656 of 21885, 274: 1382 of 20980, 275: 2304 of 13448). Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 62169 matches its orders (36208 + 25961) with no refunds against it, so that figure is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net of 48740 matches its orders (29142 + 20980) less the 1382 refund on order 274, so it checks out. Cobalt is the last customer with refunds on it (272 and 275), so I'll get its net balance next.

I checked all three net balances against the orders and refunds by hand: acme 36208+25961=62169, birch 29142+20980-1382=48740, and cobalt 21885+13448-8656-2304=24373. All match, and the refunds agree with Alpha's handoff, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 62169 is recorded and I verified the figures against the orders and refunds. Birch's net of 48740 checks out, so I'll record its payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. Cobalt's net of 24373 was already checked against its orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid, and each net balance matched my hand check against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
